text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT
- Police have sometimes used hypnosis in crime investigations, especially in cases involving violence.
- Profits of large Finnish companies expected to increase by about a third this year, according to analysts' forecasts.
- Confidential health information oabout deceased persons is indequately protected, expert says.
- Life insurance premium income tripled last year to more than seven billion markka, insurance federation estimates.
- Laws on the cultural autonomy of the Sami people of Lapland are fraught with contradictions, making changes in the statutes inevitable, legal expert says.
KAUPPALEHTI

- The Federation of Finnish Entreprises says pension insurance funds could channel about a billion markka into small and medium-sized firms this year, and suggests a separate fund to grant guarantees.
- Helsinki-Vantaa airport plans further 350 million markka terminal expansion.
- Amended corporations act strengthens small shareholders' rights to receive information and to ask questions of management.
- Stockholm Energi CEO Thomas Bruce says experiences in Norway and Britain show declining margins for power producers in liberalised markets.
DEMARI
- Interest in Lenin still alive in Russia as 353 Russians visited the Lenin museum in Finnish town of Tampere last year.
AAMULEHTI
- Defence Forces shifting to new system of fixed-term appointments for high officers -- maximum term five years.
- Almost 60 banks out of a total of 300 could drop out of the cooperative banking group due to opposition to plans to make it function like a commercial bank.
- Central Organisation of Finnish Trade Unions SAK backs woman lawyer to succeed Jorma Reini as state labour mediator.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Cultor's Finnsugar Bioproducts unit has found markets for substance which is said to relieve stress in animals when added to feed.
- Foreign Ministry has rejected claims for compensation from Finnish citizen who says he was kidnapped in Siberia in 1994 and that Finnish officials failed to help him recover ransom.
